measures.label: Item sales
measures.formula_text: Sum of order subtotal (item price x quantity, before shipping, handling and tax) for the orders whose America/New_York business date is the day, per marketplace.
measures.sql: SELECT business_date, channel, count(*), round(sum(subtotal), 2), round(sum(coalesce(shipping_charged, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(marketplace_fees, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(refund_amount, 0)), 2) FROM fct_orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
measures.notes: This is what the page calls revenue. Test and canceled orders are excluded upstream. Column 'item_sales (round(sum(subtotal), 2))' of the statement; written to artifact/data/daily__all.json (cols: date, channel, orders, item_sales, shipping, fees, refunds). SQL taken verbatim from tools/export_artifact_docs.py: True.

measures.label: Orders
measures.formula_text: Count of kept orders per business date and marketplace.
measures.sql: SELECT business_date, channel, count(*), round(sum(subtotal), 2), round(sum(coalesce(shipping_charged, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(marketplace_fees, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(refund_amount, 0)), 2) FROM fct_orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
measures.notes: One row per order, not per item. Column 'orders (count(*))' of the statement; written to artifact/data/daily__all.json (cols: date, channel, orders, item_sales, shipping, fees, refunds). SQL taken verbatim from tools/export_artifact_docs.py: True.

measures.label: Shipping charged
measures.formula_text: Sum of shipping charged to the buyer on those orders (handling is separate and not included).
measures.sql: SELECT business_date, channel, count(*), round(sum(subtotal), 2), round(sum(coalesce(shipping_charged, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(marketplace_fees, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(refund_amount, 0)), 2) FROM fct_orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
measures.notes: Money the buyer paid for shipping, not what Goodwill paid the carrier. Handling is channel-dependent: ShopGoodwill reports Handling in its own column (fct_orders.handling, NOT in this measure), while eBay and GoodwillFinds send one delivery field that already includes handling (so it IS in this measure). Column 'shipping (round(sum(coalesce(shipping_charged, 0)), 2))' of the statement; written to artifact/data/daily__all.json (cols: date, channel, orders, item_sales, shipping, fees, refunds). SQL taken verbatim from tools/export_artifact_docs.py: True.

measures.label: Marketplace fees
measures.formula_text: Sum of marketplace and payment fees on those orders, positive = cost. Shipping labels are not included.
measures.sql: SELECT business_date, channel, count(*), round(sum(subtotal), 2), round(sum(coalesce(shipping_charged, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(marketplace_fees, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(refund_amount, 0)), 2) FROM fct_orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
measures.notes: Fees sit on the order's own date, not the date the fee was posted. Column 'fees (round(sum(coalesce(marketplace_fees, 0)), 2))' of the statement; written to artifact/data/daily__all.json (cols: date, channel, orders, item_sales, shipping, fees, refunds). SQL taken verbatim from tools/export_artifact_docs.py: True.

measures.label: Refunds
measures.formula_text: Sum of refund dollars attributed to the order they belong to, so a refund lands on the ORDER's business date.
measures.sql: SELECT business_date, channel, count(*), round(sum(subtotal), 2), round(sum(coalesce(shipping_charged, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(marketplace_fees, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(refund_amount, 0)), 2) FROM fct_orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
measures.notes: Differs from fct_refunds and the month-end close, which date a refund by when the money went back. Column 'refunds (round(sum(coalesce(refund_amount, 0)), 2))' of the statement; written to artifact/data/daily__all.json (cols: date, channel, orders, item_sales, shipping, fees, refunds). SQL taken verbatim from tools/export_artifact_docs.py: True.

measures.label: Average order
measures.formula_text: item_sales divided by orders over the selected days and marketplaces (ratio of sums, not an average of daily averages).
measures.sql: SELECT business_date, channel, count(*), round(sum(subtotal), 2), round(sum(coalesce(shipping_charged, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(marketplace_fees, 0)), 2), round(sum(coalesce(refund_amount, 0)), 2) FROM fct_orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
measures.notes: Computed in the page from the daily doc: sum(item_sales) / sum(orders). No separate SQL; zero orders gives 0.

measures.label: Store revenue

measures.sql: WITH ev AS ( SELECT strftime(timezone('America/New_York', identified_at_utc), '%Y-%m') m, store_id, category, 1 id, 0 se, 0 li, 0 su, 0.0 rv FROM fct_items WHERE identified_at_utc IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT strftime(timezone('America/New_York', manifested_at_utc), '%Y-%m'), store_id, category, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0.0 FROM fct_items WHERE manifested_at_utc IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT strftime(timezone('America/New_York', first_listed_at_utc), '%Y-%m'), store_id, category, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0.0 FROM fct_items WHERE first_listed_at_utc IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT strftime(business_date, '%Y-%m'), store_id, category, 0, 0, 0, quantity, sale_price FROM fct_order_lines) SELECT m, coalesce(store_id, ''), coalesce(category, ''), sum(id), sum(se), sum(li), sum(su), round(sum(rv), 2) FROM ev WHERE m >= '2025-09' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1, 2, 3

SELECT date_trunc('month', business_date)::DATE m, SUM(subtotal), SUM(marketplace_fees) FROM fct_orders WHERE business_date >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND business_date < DATE '2026-10-01' GROUP BY 1

SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('month', business_date)::DATE FROM fct_orders
measures.notes: Code definition (goodwill_pulse/kpi.py): Total e-commerce revenue: Σ item subtotal (fct_orders.subtotal; under a store/category filter Σ fct_order_lines.sale_price credited to the originating store), excl. shipping, handling and tax. measures.label: Top 10 categories by margin
measures.formula_text: Rank categories by gross profit $. Value = the #1 category's gross profit; `breakdown` holds the top 10
measures.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT category FROM fct_order_lines WHERE category IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1

SELECT date_trunc('month', business_date)::DATE m, SUM(sale_price), SUM(fee_alloc) FROM fct_order_lines WHERE business_date >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND business_date < DATE '2026-10-01' AND category = 'Art' GROUP BY 1

SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('month', business_date)::DATE FROM fct_orders

WITH s AS (SELECT order_key, SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Art' THEN sale_price ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(sale_price), 0) AS share FROM fct_order_lines GROUP BY order_key) SELECT date_trunc('month', r.business_date)::DATE m, SUM(r.amount * s.share) FROM fct_refunds r JOIN s USING (order_key) WHERE r.business_date >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND r.business_date < DATE '2026-10-01' GROUP BY 1

SELECT count(*) FROM fct_fees WHERE fee_type IN ('shipping_label')

WITH s AS (SELECT order_key, SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Art' THEN sale_price ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(sale_price), 0) AS share FROM fct_order_lines GROUP BY order_key) SELECT date_trunc('month', x.business_date)::DATE m, SUM(x.amount * s.share) FROM fct_fees x JOIN s USING (order_key) WHERE x.fee_type IN ('shipping_label') AND x.business_date >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND x.business_date < DATE '2026-10-01' GROUP BY 1
measures.notes: Code definition (goodwill_pulse/kpi.py): Top 10 categories by margin: categories ranked by gross profit $ (revenue − fees − shipping labels − refunds, lines credited by category). Value = gross profit of the #1 category; the card carries the ranked top-10 list in ``breakdown``. Pillar profitability; better when up; availability built; star=False; scorecard=True. measures.label: Listings created
measures.formula_text: count of items whose **first** listing (any channel) started in the month; relists are excluded
measures.sql:
WITH first_l AS ( SELECT sku, min(listed_at_utc) AS fl, arg_min(channel, listed_at_utc) AS channel, arg_min(store_id, listed_at_utc) AS store_id, arg_min(category, listed_at_utc) AS category FROM fct_listings WHERE sku IS NOT NULL AND listed_at_utc IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sku), first_sale AS ( SELECT l.sku, min(o.paid_at_utc) AS sold_at FROM fct_order_lines l JOIN fct_orders o USING (order_key) WHERE l.sku IS NOT NULL GROUP BY l.sku) SELECT date_trunc('month', (fl_.fl AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'))::DATE m, count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.sold_at >= fl_.fl AND s.sold_at <= fl_.fl + INTERVAL 30 DAY), avg(epoch(fl_.fl - i.identified_at_utc)) / 86400.0, avg(epoch(fl_.fl - i.manifested_at_utc)) / 86400.0, max(fl_.fl) FROM first_l fl_ LEFT JOIN first_sale s USING (sku) LEFT JOIN fct_items i ON i.item_id = fl_.sku WHERE date_trunc('month', (fl_.fl AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'))::DATE BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-01' GROUP BY 1

SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('month', (listed_at_utc AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'))::DATE FROM fct_listings
measures.notes: Code definition (goodwill_pulse/kpi.py): Listings created: items whose FIRST listing (any channel) started in the month; relists not counted. SELECT date_trunc('month', business_date)::DATE m, SUM(amount) FROM fct_refunds WHERE business_date >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND business_date < DATE '2026-10-01' GROUP BY 1

SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('month', business_date)::DATE FROM fct_orders

SELECT date_trunc('month', business_date)::DATE m, SUM(subtotal), SUM(marketplace_fees) FROM fct_orders WHERE business_date >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND business_date < DATE '2026-10-01' GROUP BY 1
measures.notes: Code definition (goodwill_pulse/kpi.py): Refund rate: refunds $ (by refund date) ÷ revenue. Pillar engagement; better when down; availability built; star=False; scorecard=False. SQL recorded by running compute() for 2026-09 against harmonized.duckdb; month cards also run the same statements for the prior month, prior year and a 13-month trend with other date parameters. Statements that only select distinct months decide whether a month is covered by a table (a covered month with no rows is a real 0, an uncovered month is None).
